Connection · 2h01

Fly3h12AUS to BOS
7:44p
Land Terminal A · off by 8:00
Row 3 gets you out ahead of the cabin. Do not linger — international boarding starts 45 to 60 minutes before 9:45, so the gate deadline is 8:45. That is 45 usable minutes, not two hours.
Shuttle20–40minairside, no re-screening
8:00p
Delta airside shuttle to Terminal EThe plan
Take the shuttle. It is the only choice you can still reverse.
Delta runs a shuttle exclusively for passengers connecting domestic Terminal A to international Terminal E. You never leave security, so the Terminal E checkpoint stops mattering — and at 8 PM that checkpoint is the evening international bank.
Ask a Delta agent where it boards. Sources give both Gate A11 and gates A17–A18; do not walk the wrong end of the concourse on a guess.
Skybridge through Central Parking, then security at E
Fifteen to twenty minutes of indoor moving walkways, plus whatever the Terminal E queue costs. Sky Priority helps. Massport is blunt that A has no post-security link and advises allowing 45–60 minutes for Terminal A connections. Viable, but only decide this after checking the shuttle — once you are landside you cannot get back to it.
~8:20p
Air France Lounge, Terminal E
Redesigned 2025, open until 11:30 PM. Delta Sky Club and the Delta One Lounge near Gate E13 are also in E. Only if the transfer runs clean — the gate matters more than the lounge.

The park

Bon Marché · Luxembourg · the river · by bike
Open the ride in Maps
↗
Bike20min
9:45a
Lime e-bikesSuggested
Matt’s biggest piece of advice: buy the pass and ride. Sunday also closes the riverside roads to cars.
Buy the LimePass on arrival. Two hundred minutes, good for a month, and better value than unlocking each bike one at a time. Minutes are per account and a Group Ride deducts for each rider, so 200 is really 100 minutes of the two of you moving — still enough for the Left Bank block and a couple of dinner runs.
Free-floating, so there are no docks — find the nearest bike in the app. One phone unlocks both, up to five.
Rue de Rivoli is the spine. Fully protected, two-way, and rue de la Verrerie feeds straight onto it.
Do not ride home from dinner. France applies the same alcohol limits to cyclists as to drivers. Bike out, taxi back.
Four rides, not one. The pause caps at fifteen minutes, which covers the Grande Épicerie but not Bon Marché and certainly not three hours in the Luxembourg. End the ride at each stop and take a fresh bike after.
Park on a blue pin only. Ending outside a zone, or blocking a footpath, carries a penalty. You photograph the parked bike to close the ride, so leave yourself a minute for it.
Get the app

The oldest department store in the world, 1852.
The only one Parisians actually shop in. Go for the building and the top-floor light as much as the racks.

Morning

7:30a
River loop · 6 kmSuggested
Île Saint-Louis, the left bank quais, home along the car-free lower quai.
Out to the Seine at Pont Louis-Philippe, round the island on Quai d’Anjou and Quai de Bourbon, across at Pont de la Tournelle. West along the left bank past the Institut and the Orsay, back over Pont Royal, then east through the Parc Rives de Seine below the Louvre and home at Hôtel de Ville. Flat, with a few flights where you drop to the lower quai.
Go before eight. The quais fill from nine and the lower level stops being runnable. Light showers are forecast early, clearing by midday. Stretches of the island are cobbled, so stay upstairs if you are not in proper trainers.
Check before you go: the lower quai closes when the Seine runs high.

Ten stops · 35 min walking

Walk20min

Vieille du Temple → Elzevir → Beaumarchais
A single sweep east, then north. About 35 minutes of walking across the whole run, and nothing is more than six minutes from the next thing.
  • GrandCœur · 41 rue du Temple · lunch ends here at 2:30. Head east.
  • Dover Street Market · 35 rue des Francs Bourgeois · laid out like a gallery, Monday 11–7. Brian and Matt
  • Lemaire · 1 rue Elzevir · the Marais flagship by Parc Royal, daily 11–7:30. Soft tailoring and the croissant bag. Ask for Andrea or Nathan.
  • Fragments · 76 rue des Tournelles · coffee and homemade pastries. Order the carrot cake. Cash preferred.
  • Rue de Turenne · a street of luxury vintage rather than one shop. AMI sits at no. 96. Wander it, don’t plan it. Bri
  • Merci · 111 bd Beaumarchais · through the courtyard past the red Fiat, Monday 10:30–7:30. Bookshop and café in the basement. Matt
  • Vieille du Temple · Officine Générale at 106, ask for Jérôme, and A.P.C. six doors up at 112. Brian
  • Drôle de Monsieur · 28 rue de Poitou · Monday 11–7. They bring you a small espresso while you look.
  • Marché des Enfants Rouges · 39 rue de Bretagne · the oldest covered market in Paris, 1628. Closed Mondays — walk past it, not into it.
  • The Broken Arm · 12 rue Perrée · concept store and café in one. Reopens 25 August after the summer break. Stop for a café crème before turning back.
  • Rojo · 8 rue de Beauce · opens 3:30, runs to 1 AM. Spanish, dim, cocktails and wine. Where the shopping ends. Bri

Evening · candlelight

Saint-Éphrem · Notre-Dame · Café Charlot
Open the route in Maps
↗
Métro15min
7:00p
Seated at Saint-ÉphremBooked
Église Saint-Éphrem-le-Syriaque, 17 rue des Carmes, 75005. Métro Maubert-Mutualité (10), Jussieu (7) or Luxembourg (RER B).
Show the voucher at the front desk — printed or on the phone. Arrive by 7:00: they ask for thirty minutes, seating is first come first served, and late arrival does not guarantee entry. Carry coins for the usher; the pourboire is customary here. No air conditioning.
7:30p
Chopin by candlelight — Pieces from The Pianist
Elio di Tanna at the piano, seventy-five minutes, no interval. Selections from the Polanski soundtrack: the Ballade No. 1 and the C-sharp minor Nocturne, the pieces that carry the film. Young players from the Conservatoire National Supérieur, a Baroque portal, and a room lit entirely by candles.
Walk9min
8:45p
Notre-Dame
Nine minutes on foot, and the timing is the point — sunset lands at 8:36, so you arrive as the west front turns from gold to floodlit. Open again since December 2024. Then the quais east as the city switches on.
Walk16min
9:30p
Café CharlotSuggested
Rue de Bretagne. Zinc bar, red banquettes, a terrace on the corner since the thirties. An omelette, a steak-frites, a carafe — the right weight after a concert and a walk.

Drive to Les BauxCar to book
Fifteen minutes south from Saint-Rémy, and the village is on the road home. Park below and walk up — the castle entrance is at the highest point and can only be reached through the village.
Walk5min
12:00p
Château des BauxTicket at the gate
Seven hectares of ruin on a rock spur, carved into the limestone and inhabited since the Neolithic. The keep, the Sarrasine and Paravelle towers, cave dwellings, the chapel, the bakery, a dovecote and a cistern. The panorama runs to Aix, Arles and the Camargue on a clear day. Audio guide included in seven languages; reckon on one to two hours. Some of the high sections are genuinely exposed.
2:00p

Nothing on the castle site itself — the restaurants are down in Les Baux. Then five minutes home for the last afternoon by the pool.

Packing

Built around the three things this trip actually demands: a cool Paris evening, a hot Provence afternoon, and two nights of formalwear four days apart.

These two outfits carry the trip. Everything else is flexible.

  • Friday — black tie, Carrières des Lumières. The quarry holds around 60–65°F and reads damp regardless of the 82° outside. This is the one night a full jacket is a comfort, not a burden.
  • Quarry flooring is uneven stone. Worth a word to MK on footwear — heels and gravel-cut limestone don't agree.
  • Saturday — summer formal, Provence Disco. Linen suit and the terracotta shirt, as planned. On-property, so no transport buffer needed.
  • One light layer for Saturday's small hours. The party runs late and the terrace drops to the low 60s.
  • Garment bag or a proper fold — the Boston connection is 2h01 with a terminal change, so anything checked is exposed.

Mid-to-upper 70s by day, high 50s by night. The gap is the whole packing brief.

  • An unstructured jacket or overshirt that works over dinner clothes — the Notre-Dame walk and the ride home from Montmartre are after dark and exposed.
  • A packable rain shell. August storms in Paris come as short afternoon systems, not all-day rain.
  • Shoes that survive Marais cobbles and still read well at Septime.
  • Swim shorts for the Grand Mazarin indoor pool.
  • Gym kit for Neoness on Tuesday. Flat-soled shoes rather than lifting shoes — one barbell day doesn't justify them, and Converse double as walking shoes.

Low-to-mid 80s and dry, with a 20-degree drop after sunset.

  • Linen and light cotton in volume. Five days, mostly outdoors, laundry not guaranteed.
  • Real sun protection. Arles has almost no shade between LUMA and the Fondation, and the light is famously unforgiving.
  • A hat you'd actually wear. Sunglasses that survive being sat on.
  • Mistral insurance: one windproof layer. Arles and Les Baux sit directly in its path down the Rhône valley, and a two-day blow makes an 80° evening feel 15° colder.
  • Sturdy shoes for the castle — seven hectares of uneven limestone, and some of it exposed.
  • Pool days: two swim options, since one will always be drying.
  • Anything you'd want for the hotel bikes.
  • EU Type E/C adapters, 230V — at least two, plus a multi-port charger.
  • Everything essential in the carry-on. The Boston terminal change gives checked bags a real chance to miss the connection.
  • Passports and booking confirmations saved offline to the phone.
  • Medications in the cabin, not the hold.
  • A change of shirt in the carry-on for the CDG morning — you land at 10:35 AM and won't see the room until nearly 1 PM.
  • 3:30 AM pickup on the last morning. Cases by the door and clothes laid out the night of the 6th — there is no version of that morning with room to think.
  • Concert vouchers saved offline on both phones, and coins for the usher at Saint-Éphrem.

Three of the six sessions run at Hameau des Baux, which Laura confirms has a bike, a treadmill, and a bench with weights — plus a jogging trail beside the canal. Better than assumed. The small things still carry more weight than usual.

  • Resistance bands — one light, one mini loop. Highest-value item in the bag. The shoulder warm-up and the glute work both depend on them, and they weigh nothing.
  • Creatine, 5g daily — including travel days. Pre-portion it or bring the tub. Eleven days off is the one thing here that shows.
  • Flat-soled shoes. Converse or similar. Covers the Tuesday gym session and walks all day.
  • Lacrosse or massage ball — shoulder and hip maintenance after the long flights.
  • Jump rope. Five minutes is a complete warm-up anywhere.
  • Leave at home: lifting shoes, belt, straps.
